newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals firmer in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals firmer in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Tokyo precious metals futures settled slightly firmer on Friday, buoyed by firmer spot prices and the dollar's slight rebound against the yen, traders said.
Activity was lacklustre, as uncertainty over the currency market kept private investors on the sidelines.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to seven yen per gram higher. Benchmark October was up five yen at 1,355 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $378.90/379.40 per ounce at 0735 GMT, against $378.75/379.25 in New York on Thursday.

"After private investors hunted for bargains actively in gold futures on Thursday, they were wary of fresh buying. Growing views that the dollar remains vulnerable on the downside is undermining market sentiment," one trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold moved within tight ranges.
Traders remained bearish on gold, as producer selling from Australia and fragile physical demand in Asia is expected to help cap any rallies.
Platinum futures ranged from six yen to 11 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark October contract was eight yen higher at 1,374 yen.

Despite today's gains in platinum futures, the Japanese platinum market is likely to be pressured in the near future by massive long positions still held by private investors in yen-based platinum futures, traders said.
They said private investors were especially long in the December platinum contract.
Silver futures ranged from 0.9 yen to 3.3 yen per 10 grams higher. Benchmark October was up 3.0 yen at 178.0 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from one to nine yen per gram firmer, with benchmark October ending up three at 425 yen.
